messages:
helena (customer): Hey team — starting ~03:18 UTC our calls to the hosted inference endpoint are intermittently failing with 502/504s. Happening across multiple regions. Example curl output from one pod:

curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' \n  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate  
* About to connect() to api.redwood-inference.com port 443 (#0)
*   Trying 198.51.100.23...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* connect to 198.51.100.23 port 443 failed: Operation timed out
* Failed to connect to api.redwood-inference.com port 443: Operation timed out
* Closing connection 0
curl: (7) Failed to connect to api.redwood-inference.com port 443: Operation timed out

Also saw a few 502s with X-Req-Id: req_8a3b2c. We were fine before ~03:15. Any known cert work or infra changes?

mike_support: Hi @helena — sorry for the disruption. We saw a certificate rotation job around 03:16 UTC for the edge CDN cert chain. I'm opening an escalation. Can you paste a failing request's trace-id (X-Req-Id) or the app-level timestamp? Also is this from a single VPC region or multiple customer regions?

helena (customer): Trace was req_8a3b2c (attached). Failures from our us-east and eu-west AZs. Happens for a subset of requests, not all, and often retries succeed after 2-3s.

anya_ops: Thanks. I can confirm we rotated the edge certs at 03:16 UTC to swap to a new chain for the new CA. We expected a short live traffic dip during distro, but not this pattern. I'm collecting handshake logs now.

kevin_dns_sre: echoing — we also observed a burst of DNS lookups returning two different A records sets around the same time. Some resolvers returned the old IPs, some returned the new ones. TTLs were 300s for the CNAME and 60s for the final A in some intermediate caches. Dumping quick dig outputs below:

# dig +short api.redwood-inference.com @8.8.8.8
198.51.100.23

# dig +short api.redwood-inference.com @208.67.222.222
203.0.113.45

kevin_dns_sre: This TTL mismatch during the cert rotation means clients were hitting an IP whose edge had the new cert chain while the regional resolver directed them to an old node expecting the previous chain. Results: TLS handshake fails / timeouts or connection closes.

anya_ops: grabbing an example TLS handshake trace from the edge: (trimmed)

--- tcpdump snippet ---
15:03:17.123456 IP 10.4.5.6.443 > 10.2.3.4.52344: Flags [S.], seq 12345, ack 67890
15:03:17.124000 TLS 1.3 Handshake, ClientHello
15:03:17.300000 TLS 1.3 Alert (fatal): handshake_failure
15:03:17.300100 RST
--- end ---

anya_ops: Also seeing openssl client retries timing out:

openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com -timeout 5
CONNECTED(00000003)
write:errno=110

mike_support: That aligns with helena's curl timeouts. If some resolvers route to nodes with mismatched cert config, handshake will fail or stall until TCP times out.

helena (customer): Is this something customer side can mitigate while you work on it? Our app is getting throttled by 3rd-party retries and triggering alerts.

kevin_dns_sre: Short-term mitigations we recommend for customers: 1) switch to our regional endpoint (regional-us.redwood-inference.com) which is not behind the CDN rotation and has consistent IPs, 2) add exponential backoff and jitter on TLS-level failures (handshake_failure / connection timeout), 3) prefer DNS over HTTPS (DoH) or a reliable resolver to reduce stale cache variance.

anya_ops: On our side we're doing three things now: A) we pushed a targeted rollback to the previous cert chain on edges that still show >10% failed handshakes, B) we're purging CDN and edge resolver caches (in batches) to remove stale A records, C) coordinating with our DNS provider to ensure authoritative TTLs are honored and not re-serving old glue for in-flight queries.

deploy-bot: deploy 1972467921-cdncert-rotate started by anya_ops at 03:16:22 UTC
ops-bot: alert tls-handshake-failures > 5% in api-edge-prod triggered at 03:19:05 UTC

mike_support: Status update for @helena — we rolled back the cert chain on five problematic PoPs at 03:34 UTC. Early telemetry shows handshake error rate dropped from 18% to ~2% across your observed traces. We're continuing cache purges; full propagation expected in ~10 minutes. Can you confirm whether your retries decreased after 03:34?

helena (customer): Confirmed — our error rate dropped significantly after 03:36 in our logs. Thanks. A couple follow-ups: 1) will you provide a postmortem? 2) any recommendations to avoid this in future?

anya_ops: Absolutely — we'll open a postmortem and share within 48 hours. Immediate action items: - revert the cert rollout plan to use blue/green host pinning next time (avoid partial chain swap across PoPs), - add a preflight probe that validates TLS chain from multiple public resolvers before marking rotation complete, - add a DNS-monitoring alert for when different resolvers return inconsistent address sets for the same name.

kevin_dns_sre: Longer term: shorten cert-rollout window to a single atomic swap at the CDN control plane, and coordinate TTL reductions 5 minutes before rotation to avoid stale caches. Also adding an automated cache-bust CNAME pattern when swapping certs.

mike_support: For your immediate incident ops: any customers still seeing issues, try the regional endpoint and we can whitelist traffic to bypass CDN routing until we complete the fix. Also if you can share a failing req_id, we'll pull the edge trace.

helena (customer): We'll try regional endpoint as a config knob for the short term. Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please include the DNS resolver dig outputs in the postmortem.

anya_ops: Will do. We'll follow up with a full timeline + root cause + remediation steps. Tagging this resolved for now pending postmortem. :white_check_mark:
